description: Formal capability catalog for perry-wit AOT TypeScript compiler targeting WASI Preview 2

tiers.name: Tier 1: Web Standard Primaries
tiers.description: Universal web and ECMAScript primitives available without environment-specific imports

tiers.name: Tier 2: Node Core Builtins
tiers.description: Node.js platform primitives mapped to WASI Preview 2 host capabilities

tiers.name: Non-Goals
tiers.description: Features explicitly excluded from AOT WebAssembly compilation

capabilities.name: Native P3 Filesystem Metadata and Directories
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: statSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, unlinkSync, rmdirSync, and readdirSync
invariants: Shared normalized longest-prefix preopens confine paths and symlinks; mutation cannot remove preopen roots
Stats preserve unsigned file sizes, signed modification milliseconds, type predicates, and identity
Directory listings materialize UTF-8 names, omit dot entries, and await the separate producer completion after EOF
Options and argument effects precede validation and I/O; known duplicate fields use the last value
Stats, string arrays, and suspended directory buffers survive helper calls, collection, and retained Promise outcomes
Normal and recoverable-error paths release descriptors, entry streams, and completion futures
differences: The default CLI remains on the legacy pipeline until R9

Reusable plain option objects retain aliases, mutation, deletion, and field effects; stat supports bigint false and throwIfNoEntry true, and readdir supports UTF-8 encoding, recursive false, and withFileTypes false
mkdirSync, unlinkSync, and rmdirSync only accept omitted or undefined options
Directory order is host-defined, materialization uses memory proportional to contents, and absent modification timestamps return zero
Component Stats use the exported stats record and stats-kind enum; string arrays use list<string>, also inside numeric-error Result returns
Errors use one-based WASI 0.3 ordinals; existsSync returns false on filesystem errors, while host traps and cancellation require store disposal

capabilities.name: Native P3 Filesystem Reads
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: readFileSync with omitted, literal, or runtime string encoding
invariants: Binary reads preserve arbitrary bytes and return independent mutable views
Text reads preserve BOMs, NULs, and valid UTF-8 with scalar string semantics
The shared transfer loop handles partial input and closure; successful EOF still awaits producer completion
Invalid options fail before I/O; read-only preopens work without requesting write permissions
Pending buffers and returned values survive collection; resources close on success and recoverable errors
Materialization uses storage proportional to file size, with multi-megabyte and repeated bounded-memory fixtures
String-or-byte kinds survive aliases, assignments, control flow, retained Promise outcomes, and component parameters/results
differences: The default CLI remains on the legacy pipeline until R9
Runtime string encodings return string-or-byte values; methods, indexing, and type-specific arguments require typeof narrowing
Component unions use the exported text-or-bytes variant with text(string) and bytes(list<u8>) cases
Plain option objects support encoding and the default or r flag, preserve current fields through helpers and mutation, and return a string-or-byte union when reused
Malformed text throws filesystem error 9 instead of Node replacement decoding
The binary encoding label returns Uint8Array, preserving the existing compiler contract; Node returns Latin-1 text for that label
Host traps and cancellation require store disposal

capabilities.name: Native P3 Filesystem Writes
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: overwrite-only writeFileSync from fs and node:fs
invariants: Named aliases, namespace imports, and default imports retain binding identity; unused imports add no filesystem capability
String data preserves exact UTF-8 and NUL bytes; Uint8Array data writes only its visible range
Arguments and plain object fields execute in source order; aliases, mutation, deletion, and duplicate-field effects survive validation and collection
Invalid encodings, flags, and unknown option properties fail before opening or truncating a file
Normalized paths select the longest matching preopen on a component boundary; symlink resolution remains host-confined
Shared native stream writes preserve partial transfers and await an independent filesystem completion
Descriptors, writable ends, and completion futures close on normal and recoverable-error paths; suspended buffers survive sibling collection
differences: The default CLI remains on the legacy pipeline until R9
Options accept encoding strings, null, undefined, and reusable plain objects; getters, setters, methods, spreads, computed literal keys, and custom prototypes are diagnosed
Only the default or w flag is supported; UTF8 labels accept ASCII case, and binary encoding is restricted to byte data
Errors throw the one-based WASI 0.3 filesystem error ordinal; already written bytes are not rolled back
Host traps and cancellation require store disposal; plain objects remain guest-internal with nonrecursive structural types or simple interfaces

capabilities.name: Native P3 Output
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: perry:stdio byte writes and single-string console logging
invariants: writeStdout and writeStderr preserve arbitrary bytes and visible Uint8Array ranges
Shared native writes retry partial transfers and respect host backpressure
Successful transfer still awaits the separate capability completion future
console.log routes to stdout; console.error and console.warn route to stderr, preserving UTF-8 and embedded NULs and appending a newline
Output buffers remain traced while suspended, including collection by sibling tasks
Normal and recoverable error paths close writable ends and consume and drop completion futures
differences: The default CLI remains on the legacy pipeline until R9
Byte writes must be immediately awaited; console calls return void but may suspend for host output
Console supports exactly one string; formatting and other argument forms are diagnosed
Output errors throw numeric codes: 1 I/O, 2 invalid byte sequence, 3 broken pipe; already written bytes remain visible
Host traps and cancellation require store disposal; returned streams and callbacks need further ownership support

capabilities.name: Scalar UTF-8 Text
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: UTF-8 text operations and component string boundaries
invariants: Length, indexing, slicing, search positions, and string iteration count Unicode scalars
String for-of evaluates its input once and retains that snapshot across mutation and P3 waits
Nested loops preserve update effects and route break/continue through crossed finally clauses
Unicode case conversions, code-point construction, split, and join preserve valid UTF-8
Literal regex search uses immutable compiled tables, returns reusable scalar positions, and allocates no guest storage
Canonical boundaries retain byte lengths; completed serial calls reclaim their invocation storage
differences: The default CLI remains on the legacy pipeline until R9
Unpaired surrogate escapes and UTF-16 code-unit APIs are diagnosed
Custom iterator protocols, labeled loop exits, and JSON remain unsupported on this path
Regex support is literal string.search with u/s flags; constructors, stored regex values, other flags, lookaround, backreferences, and property escapes are diagnosed
Implicit string coercions are restricted; traced loop collection reclaims dead temporaries, while returned-stream and callback owners remain incomplete

capabilities.name: Stored P3 Promise Outcomes
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: stored named async calls, waitFor, and repeated await
invariants: A source task starts eagerly and its caller continues while native P3 work is pending
Aliases preserve Promise identity and repeated awaits retain numeric, boolean, string, or void success and numeric rejection
Each native subtask result is observed and dropped once; later awaits read the retained language outcome
Typed Promise parameters share one native completion reader and wake concurrent observers in registration order
Promise records and retained strings share the serial invocation arena and are reclaimed after result copying
Guest rejection enters catch and finally at await; host traps remain outside the language error channel
differences: The default CLI remains on the legacy pipeline until R9
Stored Promises require the host's component async stackful and threading features
Promise parameters are guest-internal; callbacks, constructors, and combinators are not yet supported
Detached call statements are diagnosed; unobserved pending work or overlapping entry calls trap and require instance disposal
Traced loop collection reclaims dead strings and Promise outcomes; escaped captures and returned streams still need lifetime support

capabilities.name: Typed P3 Clock and Random Calls
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: waitFor, performance.now, Date.now, Math.random, crypto.getRandomValues, and crypto.randomUUID
invariants: Clocks and randomness use typed shared lowering plans and WASI 0.3 canonical adapters
Named and namespace imports from perry:clocks and perry:random preserve binding aliases and distinguish local shadows
Arguments execute once in source order, with clock durations converted from milliseconds to nanoseconds
Monotonic reads return fractional milliseconds and system-clock reads return signed whole epoch milliseconds
Random filling preserves byte-view identity and its visible range, validates type and the 65536-byte quota before host calls, skips empty views, and loops over P3 short reads
UUIDs use fresh random bytes with v4 version and variant bits; UUID text and filled views survive collection, retained Promises, suspension, and disposal
Clock and random imports contain only selected functions and share adapters when multiple operations use the same interface
Unused declarations add no component imports; all emitted function bodies retain their referenced dependencies
UTF-8 values, exceptions, and async invocation ownership remain shared across capabilities
Host failures trap independently of guest exception handlers
differences: The default CLI and generated WIT SDK still target the legacy pipeline; types/p3.d.ts describes these migration imports
Only direct calls and literal namespace member names are supported; dynamic lookup, capability function values, and spread arguments are diagnosed
Invalid or overflowing wait durations trap before the host call
Random destinations support Uint8Array only; invalid supported value kinds throw numeric 1 and oversized views throw 2, while other typed-array classes are diagnosed
Native random calls returning zero progress or too many bytes trap; prior writes are not rolled back
Date objects and process context are scoped separately in compiler.p3_dates and compiler.p3_context; argument-array mutation and callback timers remain open migration work
Instances support serial calls; cancellation discards the store

capabilities.name: P3 Immutable Date and Temporal Values
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: immutable UTC Date and typed Temporal.Instant / Temporal.PlainDateTime
invariants: Date.now() reads whole signed UTC epoch milliseconds from the P3 system clock
Construction requires a statically known number and preserves time clipping and invalid dates
Constructed dates have distinct object identity and aliases retain identity
getTime() returns the timestamp or NaN for invalid dates
ISO formatting covers the entire clipped range, including negative timestamps, year zero, and signed six-digit years
Invalid ISO serialization throws numeric 1 through shared catch/finally completion handling
Dates and ISO strings survive helpers, object properties, retained Promises, suspension, and repeated allocating loops under a 64 KiB guest cap
Pure epoch/ISO computations require no WASI imports
differences: The default CLI remains on the legacy pipeline until R9
Date values are guest-internal; component boundaries carry UTC ISO strings
Omitted, copy, nonnumeric, and multi-argument constructors, calendar getters, valueOf, setters, string parsing, dynamic methods, and method arguments are diagnosed
Invalid ISO errors are numeric rather than Error objects

Temporal supports ISO string factories, Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds/epochMilliseconds, PlainDateTime fields/add({days}), and toString(); bracket annotations, options, additional calendars/zones, and implicit JSON serialization are unsupported

capabilities.name: P3 JSON and Shared Guest Graphs
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: strict UTF-8 JSON parsing and compact serialization through the component boundary
invariants: Parsed objects and mixed arrays preserve primitive tags, identity, nested mutation, and retained values across helpers, collection, and native suspension
Serialization preserves ECMAScript number formatting, duplicate-key replacement and property ordering; undefined fields are omitted and undefined array elements or holes become null
Undefined root serialization returns undefined; Dates produce ISO strings or null when invalid
Numeric error codes 1, 2, and 3 report syntax, unpaired surrogate escapes, and depth/cycles through catch/finally and declared WIT errors
Checked Rust codec adapters borrow disjoint guest storage outside measured helper data/stack; allocating loops and repeated large inputs reclaim temporary graphs
Pure JSON source tasks require no WASI imports; selected text helpers and P3 capabilities share the same guest memory
differences: Strings count Unicode scalars and reject unpaired surrogate escapes
Object keys must be strings; mixed arrays support numeric/canonical index keys, numeric length changes, deletion, membership, and Array.isArray
Revivers, replacers, indentation, custom prototypes, sparse array literals, general array methods and extra array properties are unsupported
Unsupported byte-view, Stats, decoder, and Promise serialization throws numeric 12; errors are numbers rather than Error objects
Graphs remain guest-internal; component parameters/results carry JSON strings. The default CLI remains on the legacy pipeline until R9

capabilities.name: P3 Process Context
capabilities.domain: WAFFLE Rust compiler API: read-only process.env, process.argv, and process.cwd()
invariants: Only selected wasi:cli/environment@0.3.0 functions are imported and read lazily once per instance
Cached argument-array identity and valid UTF-8 values survive component returns, helper calls, retained Promises, collection, and native suspension
Retained heap roots preserve instance-local snapshots while invocation temporaries remain reclaimable
Environment and arguments are read-only; assignment, deletion, mutating methods, and bulk writes are diagnosed through aliases, casts, containers, and helper calls
Environment-only tasks do not link JSON formatting or coercion helpers

Object.keys and string-valued Object.values produce independent snapshots with integer-index keys first and other keys in insertion order; duplicate native environment keys replace values without moving their keys
JSON snapshots preserve cached environment values and parsed copies are independent
Host failures trap without running guest finally; store disposal releases pending native work
differences: Arguments use the host-provided list without synthetic Node executable/script prefixes
The initial directory defaults to / only when absent; an explicitly empty directory remains empty
Text operations count Unicode scalars
Missing environment keys return undefined; Object.values throws 12 for nonstring fields in ordinary objects
Object.assign accepts plain object targets/sources and ignores nullish sources; other primitive sources, prototypes, and spread arguments remain unsupported
All environment and argument mutation is deferred; the default CLI remains on the legacy pipeline until R9

capabilities.name: Guest Function Values
capabilities.domain: Calling synchronous guest function values with retained lexical captures
invariants: Calls arrow/function expressions and aliases of named functions through the TypeScript table while preserving Rust's separate table
Evaluates the callee and arguments once in source order, pads missing parameters with undefined, and evaluates excess arguments
Captured strings, objects, and byte views retain identity and remain alive when a callback survives across invocations
Captured object mutation is visible to callbacks; released callback graphs, including cycles, are reclaimed at invocation cleanup or between timer callbacks
Guest callback exceptions propagate to surrounding try/catch blocks
differences: Shared mutable lexical captures, this/new.target, async/generator function expressions, and rest/default/arguments parameters report compiler diagnostics
Named function values with captures and calls with spread arguments report compiler diagnostics
Timers retain callback graphs until delivery or cancellation; bound functions and array callback methods remain separate work
Guest callbacks do not change WIT export types; SDK declarations continue to describe selected WIT contracts

capabilities.name: Timers
capabilities.domain: Direct setTimeout/setInterval and clearTimeout/clearInterval calls with synchronous guest callbacks and retained arguments
invariants: Evaluates callback, delay, and extra arguments once in source order; passes the extra arguments to the callback without copying referenced values
Uses monotonic clock subscriptions in deadline order, with registration order breaking equal-deadline ties; each timeout fires once
Retains captures and arguments until delivery or cancellation, including shared objects and byte views
Clearing a pending timer releases its subscription; unknown or expired numeric IDs cannot cancel later work
Intervals keep the same numeric ID while running; either clear API can cancel a timeout or interval, including from its callback
Reclaims temporary guest values between completed callbacks while preserving captures, arguments, globals, and the enclosing function's result
An empty queue returns without polling; uncaught guest exceptions, including initialization failures, cancel pending timers before reaching the existing invocation error path
Timer-only components retain monotonic-clock and poll interfaces without wall-clock, HTTP, filesystem, randomness, or environment imports
differences: CLI and exported component invocations drive pending timers to completion before returning to the host; the synchronous function's return value is computed before callbacks run
Timer IDs are instance-local numbers and never repeat; Node Timeout objects, unref/ref, globalThis timer methods, and timer functions used as values are outside this subset
Delays use Node-style whole milliseconds: values below 1, nonfinite values, or values above 2147483647 become 1; other values are truncated
Intervals rearm from the actual callback start plus the original delay; late delivery does not replay missed ticks, and an uncleared interval keeps the invocation running
Timer function values report compiler diagnostics; callback forms follow the guest-function subset
Direct Promise constructors can resolve or reject from timer callbacks; guest microtasks run before the next timer callback

capabilities.name: Guest Async Tasks
capabilities.domain: Named guest async functions with retained locals and queued await continuations
invariants: Executes named async bodies in WebAssembly without rt:__async JavaScript imports, including functions without await
Runs the synchronous prefix immediately and queues await continuations in order for ordinary values and guest task Promises
Each async activation returns a distinct Promise and adopts a returned guest Promise's outcome
Direct global new Promise(executor) invokes the executor synchronously with callable resolve/reject functions; the first settlement wins, including while adopting another guest Promise
Timer-produced Promises resume await continuations before the next timer callback; cancellation with no runnable producer reports an error at the synchronous export boundary
Selected WIT exports drive continuations to completion and marshal the resolved task value through the existing synchronous Preview 2 ABI
Suspended cells, cyclic objects, and byte views survive continuation execution and are reclaimed after success or rejection
Generated implementation contracts accept synchronous or Promise results and reject incompatible resolved types
differences: Tests cover nested pure and timer-backed awaits, loops, string exceptions, catch/finally, scalar/string/result/unit ABI results, and bounded memory; native HTTP producer readiness remains unfinished
Async function expressions and class methods, generators, captured named functions, and rest/default/arguments parameters report compiler diagnostics
Promise static methods in programs using native async or guest constructors report diagnostics; Promise instance methods raise a guest exception
The existing guest exception bridge uses string payloads; discarded-task rejection reporting and general Promise APIs are outside this initial subset
Only direct global Promise construction is supported; constructor aliases, subclassing, arbitrary thenables, and legacy top-level await of pending timer Promises are outside the subset
Pure async continuations do not poll the host; shared cleanup still retains the WASI poll interface

capabilities.name: Object Spread Operator
capabilities.domain: Shallow object property merging ({ ...a, ...b }) with right-to-left property override semantics
invariants: Evaluates object operands left-to-right
Produces a new distinct object identity
Overwrites keys present in earlier objects with keys from later objects
Preserves string, numeric, boolean, array, and nested object property values
Shallow copies retain nested object and byte-view identity, including shared mutation
differences: Executed natively via guest runtime handle table and NaN-boxing rather than prototype lookups
Nested reference and byte-view behavior is also exercised by tests/binary_views_test.rs

capabilities.name: Console Stream Routing
capabilities.domain: Writing formatted text to standard I/O streams
invariants: console.log writes UTF-8 text to WASI stdout descriptor with a trailing newline
console.error writes UTF-8 text to WASI stderr descriptor with a trailing newline
Writes are immediately flushed to the host stream
differences: Supports string primitives directly; object inspection formats via JSON representation

capabilities.name: Promise.all Concurrency
capabilities.domain: Concurrent dispatch and collection of multiple asynchronous operations
invariants: Dispatches all operand promises concurrently without sequential blocking
Resolves with an array of resolved values preserving the original input order
Fails fast upon the first rejected promise
differences: Cooperative polling on WASIp2 event loop via wasi:io/poll rather than a JS microtask queue
Promise.all inside native guest async programs remains diagnosed until guest-task combinators are implemented

capabilities.name: WASI HTTP incoming handler
capabilities.domain: Serving buffered bodies and forwarding request streams through wasi:http/incoming-handler@0.2.6
invariants: The http-server world maps exported incomingHandlerHandle(request) to the generated resource ABI; synchronous Responses and timer-backed guest Promise<Response> results complete through the same boundary
Request method, absolute URL, read-only headers.get()/has(), body forwarding, and bounded text()/json()/bytes() are available across guest awaits
Direct global new Response accepts a string, Uint8Array, supported body stream, null, or omitted body; status and headers options are validated before acquiring outgoing resources
String bodies preserve UTF-8 and binary bodies copy the visible view; headers preserve Latin-1 bytes, validate names/values, and trim surrounding HTTP whitespace
new Response(request.body) forwards at most one 8192-byte input chunk at a time, respects output permits and flush completion, and can transmit more than the materialized-body limit
Responses are published before output; stream waits poll alongside guest timers and allow queued microtasks to run at safe frame boundaries
Request children, streams, bodies, pollables, and outparams are released on success, recoverable failures, and peer cancellation; canceled I/O also releases pending guest work
Repeated buffered/streaming calls in one instance have bounded memory after warm-up, including retained/released values, rejection, read/write/flush failures, and cancellation
differences: Materializing Request bodies or constructing byte/string Response bodies is limited to 1048576 bytes; streamed forwarding does not impose that total-size limit

Body methods materialize and cache bytes through the guest await bridge and may read repeatedly; retained materialized values remain readable, but unread incoming resources close when their invocation ends

Forwarding consumes its shared body source; stale or consumed sources raise guest exceptions. Response.body can also forward a constructed byte body. General ReadableStream readers, stream constructors, transforms, abort signals, and bodyUsed compatibility remain outside this subset
Response statusText is empty; custom statusText options, ArrayBuffer, Blob, FormData, cloning, and unsupported body methods raise diagnostics
Only the documented direct constructor/method subset is supported; ambient DOM declarations describe a broader API than this runtime implements

Awaited guest work settles before publishing the response; remaining work runs between stream readiness waits and drains before the handler returns. Uncleared intervals keep successful invocations running; failed I/O cancels them. A Promise without runnable work reports an error
Failures before response publication use the WASI outparam and become HTTP 500 in the tested host; later body failures close the stream. A failed module initializer is not retried in that instance
The pinned wasmtime serve command needs -S cli=y and -O pooling-max-tables-per-module=2 for the current runtime interfaces and TypeScript/Rust tables

capabilities.name: global.fetch
capabilities.domain: Asynchronous HTTP network requests using wasi:http/outgoing-handler
invariants: Dispatches GET, POST, HEAD, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS, and valid custom method tokens to absolute HTTP(S) URLs
Returns a Promise resolving to a Response handle
Rejects on connection refusal, DNS failure, or network timeout without crashing host
Response status, ok, url, and read-only headers.get()/has() remain available after buffered body consumption
Header lookup is case-insensitive; repeated fields are joined with comma and space, and missing fields return null
Invalid or forbidden methods and bodies on GET/HEAD fail before requests are dispatched
Uint8Array request bodies transmit only their visible bytes; Response.bytes() returns an independent byte view without UTF-8 conversion
Buffered text and JSON decode UTF-8 with replacement and remove an initial BOM while preserving cached response bytes
differences: Does not support loopback redirects, custom CA stores, or WebSocket upgrades
WASI Preview 2 does not expose a reason phrase; Response.statusText is always an empty string
Response headers support get and has; mutation and iteration APIs report unsupported methods
Method, metadata, header, binary transfer, and resource ownership behavior is exercised by tests/http_regression_test.rs
Buffered body reads can repeat from cached bytes; single-use bodyUsed semantics and streaming are not implemented
ArrayBuffer, Blob, FormData, and response cloning APIs report unsupported methods; binary bodies use Uint8Array
Post-return reclaims guest values; unreachable HTTP resources are released at the next ordinary invocation because component post-return cannot call host imports

capabilities.name: Response.prototype.json
capabilities.domain: Consuming HTTP response body stream and parsing UTF-8 JSON into typed structures
invariants: Streams incoming body chunks from wasi:http input-stream
Parses valid JSON objects, arrays, strings, numbers, and booleans
Rejects the returned Promise with a SyntaxError when body is malformed JSON
differences: Parsed structures are held in guest runtime handles and can be directly splatted or serialized

capabilities.name: process.exit
capabilities.domain: Process termination with an explicit numeric exit code
invariants: Immediately halts execution and propagates code to wasi:cli/exit@0.2.x
Code 0 denotes success; non-zero codes denote failure
differences: Does not invoke Node beforeExit or exit listener hooks

capabilities.name: performance.now and Monotonic Clocks
capabilities.domain: High-resolution monotonic time measurement using wasi:clocks/monotonic-clock
invariants: performance.now() returns monotonic time in milliseconds as a float
Values never decrease across successive calls
differences: Resolution and origin are backed by the host's wasi:clocks/monotonic-clock implementation

capabilities.name: Date and Wall Clocks
capabilities.domain: Legacy P2 CLI date support pending R9 retirement; the production contract is compiler.p3_dates
invariants: Date.now() returns whole UTC milliseconds since the UNIX epoch
Omitted arguments use current time; numeric timestamps, Date copies, and the tested null/undefined/boolean conversions preserve the supported Date semantics
getTime() and toISOString() preserve UTC epoch milliseconds; ISO formatting uses the shared datealgo dependency
Invalid Date toISOString calls raise a guest exception at the call site
differences: Legacy constructor coercions are excluded from the P3 cutover contract; calendar getters are diagnosed on both compiler paths
Date string parsing, multi-argument constructors, setters, and the remaining Date API are outside the supported subset
Detailed constructor and exception regressions run in tests/clocks_test.rs

capabilities.name: Randomness and Cryptography
capabilities.domain: Cryptographic and pseudo-random generation using wasi:random
invariants: Math.random() generates floating point numbers in [0.0, 1.0)
crypto.randomUUID() generates valid RFC 4122 v4 UUID strings
crypto.getRandomValues(view) fills and returns the supplied Uint8Array, restricted to its visible byte range
Unsupported arguments and views larger than 65536 bytes fail before host randomness is requested or bytes are mutated
differences: Only Uint8Array is supported for getRandomValues; other integer view types are not implemented
Powered by wasi:random/random and wasi:random/insecure; controlled fill, boundary, and vector tests run in tests/random_test.rs

capabilities.name: Process Environment, Arguments, and CWD
capabilities.domain: Accessing environment variables, command-line arguments, and working directory via wasi:cli/environment
invariants: process.env exposes host environment variables as a JavaScript object
process.argv exposes command-line arguments as a JavaScript string array
process.cwd() returns the current working directory string
The P3 compiler exposes read-only environment and argument snapshots; see compiler.p3_context
differences: Environment and arguments are cached guest-local snapshots; P3 context mutation is unsupported
Arguments are the host-provided WASI list without synthesized Node executable/script prefixes
Working directory is initial-cwd, with / used when the host supplies none
Read-only P3 context tests run in tests/waffle_platform/context.rs; tests/env_test.rs covers the retiring legacy path

capabilities.name: Uint8Array Byte Views
capabilities.domain: Byte construction, indexed access, and shared subviews used by randomness and filesystem APIs
invariants: Numeric lengths create zero-filled views; array/view inputs copy the visible bytes
Construction and indexed writes apply wrapping byte conversion; invalid indices do not alias valid elements
Subarrays share storage and resolve negative bounds relative to the current view
JSON serialization exposes enumerable numeric object keys
Object properties, spreads, and Object.assign preserve view identity and offset; retained object graphs keep their referenced views alive across task calls
differences: Other typed-array classes, ArrayBuffer interoperability, Node Buffer compatibility, and broader Uint8Array methods are outside the tested subset
This evidence is a Rust integration suite; the TypeScript differential report does not execute it

capabilities.name: Sandboxed Synchronous Filesystem
capabilities.domain: Synchronous file and directory operations relative to host-provided WASI preopens
invariants: UTF-8 reads/writes and raw Uint8Array reads/writes work inside supplied preopens
Byte-view writes preserve offsets, lengths, and arbitrary byte values
Directory listing, creation, removal, existence checks, and the tested size/time/type metadata are available

Unsupported write modes, binary string writes, unsupported readFileSync options, and unsupported directory/metadata options (for mkdirSync, readdirSync, statSync, unlinkSync, and rmdirSync) are evaluated and rejected before opening, querying, or mutation
differences: UTF-8 reads reject invalid UTF-8; omitted encoding returns Uint8Array; unsupported encodings, flags, or option objects are rejected before opening files
Binary encoding on reads returns a Uint8Array byte view rather than Node's legacy Latin-1 string coercion
Write support is overwrite-only; append/exclusive flags, permissions, recursive operations, and filesystem promises are unsupported
mkdirSync, readdirSync, statSync, unlinkSync, and rmdirSync evaluate arguments in standard order and reject unsupported options before preopen resolution or I/O mutation
Stats support is limited to size, mtimeMs, isFile(), and isDirectory()
This evidence is a Rust integration suite using preopened scratch directories; the TypeScript differential report does not execute it

capabilities.name: Dynamic Code Evaluation (eval / new Function)
capabilities.domain: Runtime evaluation of dynamic JavaScript strings
differences: Incompatible with AOT compilation directly to WebAssembly bytecode without embedded interpreter

capabilities.name: Child Process Spawning
capabilities.domain: Spawning arbitrary OS processes via fork / exec
differences: WASI Preview 2 does not permit unconstrained host process spawning inside the sandbox
